## Cold Read (Discovery Checklist pre-call prep)
incident.io — 82 employees, $97M raised across seed/Series A/Series B, Series B led by
Insight Partners ($62M, April 2025) at an estimated ~$400M valuation. Customers include
Netflix, Linear, Ramp, and Etsy. Engineering org runs Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
simultaneously, processing 50B+ tokens/month on development work alone (self-disclosed,
Dec 2025 blog). Published a public post in May 2026 ("Engineering teams in 2027") calling
for the org to stand up an MCP gateway and choose specialist agents deliberately — this
reads as an active build-vs-buy signal, not passive interest.

## PICS Chain (Level 1-3, from Deal Qualification Agent chart)
- **L1 Technical pain:** No shared checkpoint/session layer across their 3 concurrent
  agent tools — each tool's context dies at the tool boundary.
- **L2 Business impact:** At 50B+ tokens/month, even small per-session context loss
  compounds into real rework hours; they are already investing engineering time to build
  this unification internally (MCP gateway).
- **L3 Personal stake:** Tom Ashworth has publicly staked his internal brand on solving
  agent-handoff and skills problems well — a working solution here is a direct win for
  his mandate, not just the company's.

## Intro + Bridge
"Tom — this is [rep name]. I know this is out of the blue, so I'll be upfront: I've been
following what you and the team wrote about standing up an MCP gateway and choosing
specialist agents deliberately. Worth 15 minutes to compare notes on where that's landed
since May?"

*(Deliberately not a cold-call-script "hang up or listen" bridge — this is a warm-adjacent
open given the public content trail. Reserve the harder Bridge script for outbound with no
prior public signal.)*

## Discovery Questions
- "You mentioned wanting to unify how the team chooses and hands off between specialist
  agents — where did that project land?"
- "When a Claude Code session and a Cursor session touch the same part of the codebase,
  how does that context get reconciled today?"
- "If you could wave a magic wand and fix one thing about how sessions get reviewed after
  the fact, what would it be?"

## Objection Map (pulled from Call Prep Agent's verbatim reframe library)
| Likely objection | Reframe to use |
|---|---|
| "We're already building this ourselves (MCP gateway)" | "Makes sense — that's exactly why I reached out. Curious what's taken the most engineering time so far, and whether that's time you'd rather spend on incident response instead of agent plumbing." |
| "We don't have bandwidth to evaluate another tool right now" | "Totally fair. Out of curiosity, what's the internal MCP gateway costing you in eng time per month right now?" (quantify before pitching, per PICS sequencing rule) |

## Status Notes
- Do not lead with product. Tom already knows the problem space better than most
  prospects — treat this as a peer conversation, not a pitch. Over-explaining Entire's
  features here reads as low-status per Chad Maxim #62 ("the more you reveal credentials
  unprompted, the less experienced you look").
- If he self-diagnoses the MCP gateway's limitations unprompted, that's a "sell themselves"
  moment — let it happen, don't interrupt to pitch.
